As expected, you've lost the 1964 Election.

Despite your best efforts, perhaps it was always an impossible task to beat an incumbent as strong as Johnson from the position you began in. You were certainly never favored, so this comes as no surprise to anyone.

Despite your failure, however, the door has been opened for your followers, like Ronald Reagan, to enter Republican politics as mainstream candidates. On another note, the Southern Strategy appears to have worked in full, and Republican strategists are already taking notes on how to exploit the now wide-open South. Though your chapter may be closed, a new chapter of the Republican Party may just be beginning. In any case, your popularity in Arizona remains. Perhaps another term in the Senate is in your future?

Congratulations! You have won the 1896 election.

"The Great Commoner" will soon be President of the United States! Nobody with your political views has ever sniffed the Presidency, let alone won it, and with that in mind your supporters are rioting frenziedly in the streets. The sweetest speech of all will be your victory speech tomorrow in Lincoln, Nebraska. Prepare to enact your reform agenda and most importantly the free coinage of silver.

base/candidate_json/143@123/electoral_vi.source:
Congratulations! You have won the 1916 election.

After the tumultuous 1912, the natural supremacy of the Republican Party has reasserted itself. The next steps are up to you -- perhaps you can lead the repeal of the Adamson Act, or replace it with something more measured and comprehensive. In regards to Europe, best of luck in whatever may occur over the next four years. Finally, Wilson plans to resign before your March 4th inauguration, so that you might assume the office now.

base/candidate_json/143@123/electoral_lo.source:
Sorry, you have lost the 1916 election.

Ultimately, the popularity of Woodrow Wilson was just a little much to overcome.

It appears that Wilson's agenda will remain in effect domestically. In world affairs, it remains to be seen how the situation in Europe will finally resolve itself. As to your own prospects, it is unclear what your next steps will be. The Supreme Court seat you once enjoyed has now been lost for the foreseeable future.

1948_Truman_Barkley/questions_json/500@4.source: The Soviet Union has blocked West Berlin from receiving any supplies from Western Europe. What are your thoughts on this situation?

1948_Truman_Barkley/answers_json/3816@12.source: It's not very practical to defend West Berlin, in its isolated location, if the Soviets continue to escalate. I'd prefer to focus on building our defenses in the rest of West Germany.

1948_Truman_Barkley/answers_json/3817@13.source: We need to do whatever it takes to ensure that Berlin is adequately supplied. We cannot further embolden Soviet aggression by retreating from the agreed-upon boundaries in our 1945 settlement.

Congratulations! You have won the 1948 Presidential Election.

You have become the first Republican to win the White House in 20 years. You face a dangerous foreign situation, and your domestic agenda is likely to be opposed by Democrats and conservatives alike. 1960_Kennedy_Johnson/answers_json/3795@7.source: I support unions and I oppose the excesses of leaders such as Jimmy Hoffa. Unions, cleansed of their corrupt elements, should play a central role in the American economy.

1960_Kennedy_Johnson/answers_json/3796@7.source: We should be vigilant against labor union excesses, and the Taft-Hartley Act was a good start. I believe that we should keep that law in place.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/questions_json/291.source: Your 'Great Society' has been a major part of your campaign promises, but many potential voters are wondering how you plan to come through on some of these promises- like slashing poverty. Would you care to expand on your plans?

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1792@.source: We need to reject this endorsement right away.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/questions_json/256.source: Despite your best efforts, there’s no question about it- there’s a massive divide between the Northern, integrationist wing and the Southern, segregationist wing of the Democratic Party. Do you have a plan on bringing the two back together- at the least, for this election?

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/questions_json/254.source: Civil rights continue to be a major issue of the times, with African-American activists like MLK and Malcolm X still marching on the streets for further enforcement and expansion of the Civil Rights Act. What should be our campaign’s approach to them?

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/questions_json/266.source: Hubert Humphrey is one of the most outspoken liberals in the Democratic Party, and that reputation seems to be following him- Goldwater has recently denounced him as a 'left-extremist'. Should we step in to defend him?

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1661@.source: They have a point. The Civil Rights Act was watered down by obstruction and interference from segregationist senators, and I’d like to see one with better protections make it to my desk in my second term.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1662@.source: We’ll be sure to enforce the Act to the best of our abilities. Anything past that, I can’t. We’ll do what we need to do, whether that’s another Act or not.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1664@.source: Haven’t we done enough? The Civil Rights Act of 1964 was enough of a pain to pass. We’ve given them what they want- I can’t make any promises on legislation past that.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1712@.source: I am the candidate of stability, of safety, and of responsibility. Civil rights will be treated with the care and attention it requires under a Johnson Presidency, with no extreme actions for one side or the other.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1713@.source: I am the candidate of hope and change. In my next term, I will advance civil rights even further, and create a society that is equal in every way. On this, I give my word.

1964_Johnson_Humphrey/answers_json/1714@.source: I am the candidate of responsibility and pragmatism. Civil rights has been advanced as far as it must be- any further action will simply be federal overreach, and must be avoided. The South has nothing to fear from a Johnson Presidency.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/questions_json/254.source: Your civil rights position is the most controversial part of your campaign. Would you like to clarify your position to help ease the fears of Southern Democrats or Northern moderates?

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1661@.source: Let it be known that I side with the states on the civil rights issue. I will not change this.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1662@.source: I would like to clarify in regards to the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Despite my vote against the bill, I will uphold it as President. I would like to see it repealed- I still believe it is unconstitutional- but a President cannot ignore laws that he dislikes.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1664@.source: I would like to change my previous position. With the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, I shall make no attempt to remove this law, but I will oppose further legislation, such as mass busing or forced integration.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1714@.source: I would like to remind civil rights conscious voters that I was fighting for civil rights long before they were popular, as well as helping found the Arizona Chapter of the NAACP.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/1726@.source: Want to know who's at fault for this Civil Rights Act? It's Hubert Horatio Humphrey.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answers_json/3232@.source: We'll need to pivot left somewhat if we want to cut in on Johnson's majority. By promising to respect the Civil Rights Act and highlighting our own forwardness on the issue, we can assuage liberal fears.

1964_Goldwater_Miller/answer_feedback_js.source: This clarification helps downplay your radical reputation, while also dampening damage done to your numbers among those who are voting for your civil rights positions.

This attack will do little to help win anybody but outspoken segregationists.
Your last second switch on civil rights appeals to moderates as much as it angers Southern voters. Will they sweep you to victory?

1968_Nixon_Romney/answers_json/1700@16/d.source: The Tet Offensive was an absolute disaster for the North Vietnamese. Why should it have been prevented?

1968_Nixon_Romney/answers_json/1701@17/d.source: I'm worried that for most or all of 1967, Lyndon Johnson repeatedly assured us that the North Vietnamese were on their last legs. It's difficult to assess the situation when we can't rely on the information that we have.

1968_Nixon_Romney/answers_json/1702@18/d.source: We should have had greater security in those places where we were attacked. Let us not forget, however, that this attack greatly hurt the Viet Cong and was a victory for the United States.

1968_Nixon_Romney/answers_json/1703@19/d.source: We could have prevented the Tet Offensive entirely if we'd never entangled ourselves in this Vietnamese quagmire.

base/candidate_json/23@19/no_electoral_m.source:
Wow! No candidate holds a majority in the electoral college.

Wallace's machinations have succeeded. The election will go to the House of Representatives where the Democrats hold a clear majority.

You do hold some cards however -- Humphrey would certainly rather make concessions to you, rather than deal with George Wallace. Perhaps you could obtain a place in his Administration, or some assurances on a policy issue of your choice.

base/candidate_json/24@20/no_electoral_m.source:
Wow! No candidate achieved a majority in the electoral college.

Fortunately for you the Democrats have won a majority of the nation's Congressional delegations. Unfortunately, you also have to deal with George Wallace. He will not allow the Southern states to support any candidate who advocates desegregation.

Your best chance, sadly, is to try to broker a deal with Nixon or with other moderate Republicans.

You are the likely winner, but who knows where this all ends?

base/candidate_json/25@21/no_electoral_m.source:
Congratulations! You have deadlocked the electoral college with your votes in the South.

In a close election, your electoral votes in the South have prevented either candidate from winning a majority. Get ready to put the squeeze on Humphrey and Nixon.

Of course, you still have to deal with the possibility that Humphrey and Nixon dislike you so much that they will simply strike a deal with each other. Whatever happens, it's sure to be interesting.

base/election_json/9@4/summary.source:
George W. Bush attempts to chart a new direction for the U.S., while Al Gore tries to win election as the sitting Vice President. Ralph Nader is a leftist third-party candidate. The economy has been booming, until quite recently, but President Clinton has been through an embarrassing scandal.

Candidates will debate what to do with a $200 billion budget surplus, among other things. In the real world, Florida was decided by 537 votes after 36 days and a Supreme Court decision.

As expected, you have lost the 2000 election.

The legacy of this campaign depends on a couple of factors. First of all, did you receive 5% of the popular vote? If so, congratulations! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. Also, the Democrats were a little peeved that you "stole" votes from them in this election. Hopefully that doesn't lead to a backlash.

base/candidate_json/79@61/no_electoral_m.source:
Wow! No candidate received 270 electoral votes, but the House will elect George W. Bush as President.

Did you receive 5% of the popular vote? If so, congratulations! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. Also, the Democrats were a little peeved that you "stole" votes from them in this election. Hopefully that doesn't lead to a backlash, especially since they will lose the vote in the House.

2000_Bush_Cheney/ending/s0.l174.c12/text.source:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.

2000_Bush_Cheney/ending/s0.l178.c12/text.source:
”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!

2000_Bush_Cheney/ending/s0.l182.c9/text.source:
”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.

2000_Bush_Cheney/ending/s0.l198.c12/text.source:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

2000_Nader_LaDuke/ending/s0.l174.c12/tex.source:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.

2000_Nader_LaDuke/ending/s0.l178.c12/tex.source:
”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!

2000_Nader_LaDuke/ending/s0.l182.c9/text.source:
”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.

2000_Bush_Cheney/questions_json/355@19/d.source: The Kyoto Protocol would commit the United States (along with many other countries) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Would you support this plan as President?

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3356@38/de.source: I would not. The Protocol exempts 80% of the world, including major population centers such as China and India, from compliance, and would cause serious harm to the US economy.

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3357@39/de.source: It seems very unlikely that the Senate will ever come up with the votes to ratify this agreement. I don't know how my support or opposition would change that equation.

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3358@40/de.source: We have worked for years with many other countries to negotiate this agreement. I support the environment and believe the Protocol should be ratified.

2000_Bush_Cheney/questions_json/351@10/d.source: What are your thoughts on the USS Cole bombing, which has killed 17 American sailors. How should we prevent such incidents of terrorism in the future?

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3341@32/de.source: I support a strong, overwhelming response against whoever perpetrated this attack. Any government that harbors such terrorists should be overthrown, even if it requires the commitment of American troops.

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3342@33/de.source: We need to do two things -- first of all we need better procedures to ensure that our forces in dangerous regions do better at protecting themselves. Secondly, we will investigate who is responsible for this attack, be it Al-Qaeda or some other group, and attack them accordingly.

2000_Bush_Cheney/answers_json/3343@34/de.source: This attack was a tragedy, but it underscores the need to the United States to have a more limited foreign policy. The Cold War is over, and it doesn't make sense to deploy troops in so many parts of the world.

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!

base/candidate_json/82@64/description_as.source: John Danforth served four terms as Senator from Missouri. He has broad experience in government, and as a moderate Republican would reinforce Bush's claim to be a uniter. Danforth also has close relationships with conservative stalwarts such as Kit Bond, Clarence Thomas, and John Ashcroft, and would not arouse undue suspicion from the conservative wing of the party. Winning Missouri back would be a key piece of any Republican victory in 2000.

2012_Obama_Biden/issues_json/2@0/descrip.source: Barack Obama's signature achievement from his first term was a landmark health care reform act. The law will establish insurance exchanges which must meet minimum coverage standards, and also cannot deny people based on pre-existing conditions. To help support these policies, every American will be mandated to purchase health insurance.

2012_Obama_Biden/issues_json/2@0/stance_.source: Believes that government regulations have put an unaffordable burden on doctors and insurance companies. Supports drastic cuts to Medicare and Medicaid. May support an end to the FDA and other regulatory agencies to restore competitiveness to the American health care system.
Supports a greater role for the free market in the halth care sector. Opposed to Obamacare. Probably would not support an end to the FDA or other, more radical measures.
Probably opposed to Obamacare. Would probably support malpractice reform and other incremental measures to cut overall health care costs, without challenging the larger regulatory system.

Supports some effort to collectively insure the poor and the chronically ill. May disagree with certain aspects of Obamacare or may not support a mandate, but agrees that the current system needs more intervention.
Supports Obamacare more or less as is. Rejects calls for a public option but supports an insurance mandate and also strongly supports the existing Medicare system.

Supports Obamacare but also would support a public insurance agency to ensure minimum coverage standards are met at an affordable cost. Believes that malpractice suits are conducive to good care by providing oversight of the medical system.
Admires the attempt of Obamacare to reform the system, but sees the change as too incremental. Favors a socialized medical system on the model of most European countries.

Anyways, they explain they appear whenever a presidential election is dramatically lost, to comfort the loser, which Donald doesn't appreciate 14 minutes after losing Utah. They explain how, despite his loss, many other wonderful things will happen to him. For one, he will live a long life, as they did prior to their deaths. Trump dismisses, this, noting that he never actually actually lost, because of Sleepy Joe's massive fraud. They all sigh, and vanish into thin air next to Trump, leaving him alone in his room.
